title: Pipeline
description: Chains the modules into one workflow: which chip and protocol each module uses, who owns it and how far along it is, how it is built and what its ports look like, and the hand-offs between modules (which outlet feeds which inlet). Lives in protocols/ next to the protocols it chains; told apart by "kind": "pipeline".

variant.description: Which assay this pipeline is, e.g. capseq or tipseq (protocols/pipeline_<variant>.json).

same_as.description: protocols/pipeline_mvp.json only: the variant file it is a copy of (tools/choose_assay.py writes it; tools/validate.py fails if the two drift apart).

modules.description: In process order (the twin draws them left to right).

module.description: Pipeline id of this module, used by the hand-offs (e.g. module1, barcoding). Not necessarily the chip's id or part prefix.

status.description: final: the owner's finished design. draft: a stand-in until the owner's design lands. translated: converted by a script from another format (the chip's translated_from names the source). missing: not designed yet (a placeholder); no chip, every port TBC. bench: an off-chip bench step (a placeholder); no chip, every port TBC.

status_note.description: Shown next to the badge, e.g. 'draft – being redesigned by MJ'.

chip.description: Chip spec path. Required unless status is missing.

protocol.description: Protocol path, if the module has one in protocol format.

protocol_note.description: Where the steps live when they are not in protocol format yet.

source.description: The owner's original file when chip is a translation of it.

prefer.description: Switch automatically: if a file matching glob exists (newest by name wins), use it as the chip instead of chip, with this status. For a draft standing in for a design that is still being made.

glob.description: Relative to the repo root, e.g. chip/module2*.json.

instances.description: Several copies of the same chip, each with its own run parameters.

build.description: How the chip is made and what its ports are, so the hand-offs can flag where tubing needs an adapter.

connector.description: Port style as a short id; two modules with different ids need an adapter between them. TBC if not decided.

ports.description: Port style in words, e.g. 2 mm square holes in the 3 mm lid.

source.description: Where the method and port style are stated.

built_for_demo.description: true if this module is physically built for the dye demo; false if it exists in the twin only.

after_step.description: Step of the upstream module's protocol after which the hand-off happens.

connector.description: The two modules' build.connector values. tools/validate.py recomputes status and fails if it disagrees.

status.description: unknown when either side is TBC.

warning.description: Required for mismatch and unknown: what adapter the demo needs.

roadmap.description: Destinations after the last module (library out, sequencing). The twin draws them as end boxes.

port.description: A port id on the module's chip, or TBC when it is not known yet.

ports.description: Several ports fed by (or feeding) the same hand-off, e.g. Module 4's four inlets.

roadmap.description: A roadmap destination instead of a module port.
